title: Revenue Operations Cleanup
summary: Professionalizing CRM hygiene, pipeline discipline, forecast accuracy, handoffs, and revenue visibility.
definition: Revenue Operations Cleanup is the process of repairing the systems, rules, data, and operating cadence that govern the commercial engine.
whyItMatters: PE cares because poor revenue operations make growth unforecastable, hide pipeline risk, and weaken buyer confidence in the revenue engine.
commonProblems: CRM data is incomplete, stale, or inconsistent across reps.
Pipeline stages do not reflect real buyer progress.
Sales, marketing, customer success, and finance disagree on revenue definitions.
diagnosticQuestions: Can management explain next-quarter revenue by source, stage, probability, and owner?
Which CRM fields are required for forecast accuracy and which are noise?
Where do handoffs break between lead, opportunity, close, onboarding, and renewal?
dataNeeded: CRM opportunity, account, activity, and stage history
Bookings, revenue, churn, renewal, and expansion data
Marketing funnel and customer success handoff rules
process: Audit CRM fields, pipeline stages, definitions, and usage behavior.
Rebuild the revenue funnel from lead source through renewal.
Install forecast categories, exit criteria, and weekly pipeline inspection.
Align sales, marketing, customer success, and finance definitions.
Create dashboard and governance routines for revenue leadership.
ebitdaLogic: Better revenue operations improve forecast accuracy, sales productivity, pipeline conversion, retention visibility, and buyer confidence in repeatable growth.
caseExample: A sponsor-backed SaaS company rebuilds pipeline stages, enforces CRM hygiene, cleans renewal ownership, and raises forecast accuracy before launching a growth acceleration plan.
hundredDayPlan: Days 1-30: audit CRM hygiene, funnel definitions, and pipeline quality.
Days 31-60: reset stages, required fields, forecast categories, and handoff rules.
Days 61-100: run weekly pipeline cadence, publish dashboards, tie leadership actions to revenue movement.
commonMistakes: Treating RevOps as a Salesforce cleanup instead of an operating model repair.
Adding fields without changing management behavior.
Allowing sales leadership to override forecast rules with optimism.

articleSections.title: Establish the Funnel, Data, and Economic Baseline
body: Start by reconstructing the last four to six quarters from raw marketing, CRM, billing, product-usage, support, and renewal data. Create stable account, contact, opportunity, contract, and subscription identifiers; quantify duplicates, missing owners, stale opportunities, orphan renewals, and conflicting amounts; and reconcile closed-won bookings to billing and recognized revenue. The chief revenue officer owns commercial behavior, the CFO owns financial tie-out, and a RevOps leader owns the model. No dashboard becomes authoritative until its totals reconcile and its population, timestamp, and exclusions are documented.

Translate the funnel into volume, conversion, velocity, and economics. Suppose 10,000 monthly inquiries yield 2,000 accepted leads, 600 qualified opportunities, 180 wins, and $3.6 million of annual contract value: conversion is 20%, 30%, and 30%, with a $20,000 average contract. With an opening installed base of 1,200 customers and 85% annual logo retention, approximately 180 installed customers are lost per year, or 15 per month on average; at the current acquisition cadence, that implies 165 net logo additions per month before considering churn among newly acquired cohorts. Improving accepted-lead-to-opportunity conversion from 30% to 35% creates 100 more opportunities and, at a 30% win rate, 30 wins or $600,000 of ACV—provided capacity, implementation, and retention do not deteriorate.

Baseline cohort performance by source, segment, product, region, rep tenure, deal size, discount, and customer age. Measure stage aging, no-decision loss, sales-cycle distribution, implementation time, first-value attainment, gross and net retention, expansion, and forecast error. Averages can conceal a broken segment, so show medians and ranges. Publish a data-quality scorecard weekly during cleanup and freeze executive KPI definitions for a quarter. The first gate is not an attractive dashboard; it is a reconciled funnel in which fewer than the approved percentage of records lack required fields or violate lifecycle rules.
articleSections.callout: A revenue funnel is trustworthy only when stage populations reconcile to contracts, invoices, and renewals under stable definitions.

articleSections.title: Define the Lifecycle and Govern the Systems
body: Write one lifecycle dictionary from anonymous inquiry through renewal or churn. For every state, specify entry evidence, exit evidence, accountable owner, service level, required fields, permitted reversals, and reporting timestamp. A sales-qualified opportunity might require an identified business problem, qualified buyer, estimated value, target date, and agreed next meeting; it should not exist merely because a rep wants pipeline. Define customer, booking, go-live, active recurring revenue, expansion, contraction, renewal due, and churn with finance so pipeline, board reporting, and compensation do not use different meanings.

Govern architecture before automating. Designate the CRM as the system of action for prospects and opportunities, the contract or billing platform as authority for commercial terms, and the ERP as authority for recognized financials. Map which system creates and edits each critical field, how integrations handle failures, and who resolves exceptions. Use validation rules, picklists, deduplication, role-based access, and audit history sparingly around decision-critical data. More mandatory fields can encourage fabricated entries; require information at the point it is knowable and remove unused fields rather than preserving every legacy request.

Create a cross-functional revenue council chaired weekly for the first twelve weeks and monthly after stabilization. RevOps proposes definitions and monitors adherence; marketing, sales, implementation, success, finance, and IT approve their boundaries; the CRO adjudicates operating tradeoffs; and the CFO certifies bookings-to-revenue reconciliation. Changes require an impact note, owner, effective date, test, training plan, and dashboard version. Emergency changes expire unless ratified. This governance prevents a well-meaning administrator from silently changing a field or automation that alters forecast coverage, lead routing, renewal ownership, or executive metrics.

articleSections.title: Control Stage Conversion and Cross-Functional Handoffs
body: Instrument each handoff as an acceptance event, not an email. Marketing routes an accepted lead with source, consent, fit, and behavioral evidence; sales accepts or rejects it within a defined service level and supplies a coded reason. Closed-won requires an executed contract, validated amount, product scope, billing terms, and implementation owner. Implementation accepts only a complete package and records planned and actual go-live. Customer success receives stakeholder, use case, promise, risk, and renewal data. Renewal ownership begins well before expiration, with usage, support, payment, and value evidence visible to the account team.

Inspect conversion by cohort and diagnose the constraint before adding volume. In the 10,000-inquiry example, improving top-of-funnel volume 20% produces 36 additional wins if all rates hold, but could overload qualification and reduce acceptance quality. By contrast, recovering half of 120 monthly opportunities lost to slow follow-up could create 18 wins at the 30% rate. Test routing capacity, response time, meeting completion, proposal-to-close, implementation backlog, and early churn together. Local optimization that increases bookings while extending go-live or creating poor-fit customers transfers cost downstream rather than improving the revenue engine.

Use exception queues and gates. Leads unaccepted after twenty-four hours route to a manager; opportunities without a verified next event or beyond stage-age thresholds leave the forecast; closed-won records missing contract proof cannot enter bookings; implementations outside service level escalate to the CRO and COO; renewals without plans ninety days before expiry enter a risk review. Managers own correction, while RevOps reports recurrence by root cause. Do not allow blanket overrides. Repeated exceptions indicate bad process design, capacity mismatch, or incentive conflict and should trigger a policy or resource decision.

articleSections.title: Run Forecast Cadence and Enforce Accountability
body: Define forecast categories with evidence. Commit should require validated commercial terms, buyer process, decision path, target date, and an executable next step; best case should meet most criteria with an identified risk; pipeline is not a forecast promise. Build a weekly roll-forward showing opening forecast, stage movement, pushed and pulled deals, amount changes, wins, losses, new pipeline, and ending forecast by rep and segment. Compare submissions to actuals over time. A manager whose apparent accuracy depends on late downward revisions is not forecasting accurately and should not be rewarded for landing on the final number.

Run distinct cadences: reps and managers inspect deals weekly; the CRO, finance, and RevOps review the consolidated forecast and capacity; executives review monthly conversion, acquisition cost, implementation, retention, and expansion; the board reviews quarterly trends and scenario implications. Keep deal coaching separate from data cleanup so the meeting focuses on decisions. Managers must approve stage and forecast exceptions, marketing owns source economics, implementation owns time-to-value, success owns renewal health, and finance certifies bookings and recurring-revenue bridges. Publish actions with owners and due dates after each review.

Failure modes include mass-closing stale pipeline to manufacture improvement, overfitting stages to one sales motion, forcing excessive data entry, and treating forecast misses as rep misconduct when product, pricing, or implementation is the cause. Roll out by segment or team, train managers before reps, and compare pilot adoption and economics with a control population. Maintain office hours and a transparent issue log for four to six weeks. If users bypass the system, investigate workflow friction before adding enforcement; if leaders continue accepting spreadsheet forecasts, no amount of CRM training will change behavior.

articleSections.title: Validate Economics and Produce Exit-Grade Reporting
body: Measure benefits against the frozen baseline and separate volume, conversion, timing, and mix. If accepted-lead-to-opportunity conversion rises from 30% to 35% while lead volume and win rate remain stable, attribute incremental wins only after controlling for segment and seasonality. Track gross ACV, implementation cost, churn, discounts, and contribution margin so low-quality growth does not appear as value creation. Validate administrative savings through actual hours or avoided hires, not theoretical clicks removed. Finance signs off on revenue and margin impact; RevOps owns operating evidence; the CRO owns sustainability.

Set exit gates for the cleanup: critical-field completeness above the agreed threshold for twelve weeks, duplicate rate below tolerance, bookings reconciled monthly, stage conversion and aging stable, forecast error inside its band for at least two quarters, closed-won-to-go-live handoffs within service level, and renewal coverage complete. Once achieved, reduce the weekly council to monthly but preserve exception dashboards and quarterly definition review. If performance decays, reactivate the intensive cadence. System cleanliness is not permanent; reorganizations, acquisitions, new products, and compensation changes can quickly reintroduce ambiguity.

An exit-grade revenue package includes a lifecycle dictionary, data lineage, reconciled bookings and recurring-revenue bridges, historical funnel cohorts, forecast-versus-actual history, customer retention and expansion, implementation performance, governance minutes, and documented controls. Buyers should be able to trace a board metric from dashboard to contract and invoice and understand how the company reacts when a lead, deal, implementation, or renewal falls outside policy. That proof supports scalability and lowers key-person risk. A polished CRM demonstration without reconciliation, historical accuracy, and ownership evidence will instead deepen diligence.
